newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia, S.Africa discuss East Timor and trade.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia, S.Africa discuss East Timor and trade.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela and Indonesia's President Suharto on Tuesday discussed East Timor and also agreed to expand economic and trade ties.

"The president (Suharto) and Foreign Minister (Ali Alatas) gave an explanation to our guests about the East Timor issue," state secretary Murdiono told reporters after talks between Mandela and Suharto which lasted around two hours.
"As a friend, certainly both sides want to help in handling things that are still a hurdle for the other party," Murdiono said when asked about the East Timor discussions.
Indonesia invaded the former Portuguese colony of East Timor in 1975 and annexed it the following year. The United Nations still regards Lisbon as the territory's administering power.
"Both sides also agreed they need to expand economic and trade ties between the two countries. Therefore, there is a need to encourage the private sectors," he said.
"Both sides also agreed to set up a joint commission, at level of senior officials, aimed at boosting trade," he said.
Murdiono said South Africa wanted to learn from Indonesia's mining sector. He did not elaborate.
South Africa sought Indonesian support for its bid to host the 2004 Olympics, he added.
Mandela, who arrived in Jakarta on Monday, is scheduled to leave for Bangkok on Wednesday.
The trip is Mandela's third visit to Indonesia since his release from prison in 1990, but his first state visit.
